target_customer: Individual patients, often longevity minded, paying membership tiers of $25, $50 and $150 per month without insurance
problem: Primary care is hard to access and fragmented across labs, prescriptions and wearables; patients lack a continuous clinician that sees all their data.
business_model: consumer membership primary care practice with AI and clinician review
product_category: AI primary care and longevity practice

founders.name: George Favvas
prior_employers: Circle Medical (co-founder and CEO for over a decade)
previous_startups: Circle Medical (YC S15), grown to over $100M annualized revenue per YC page

competitors.name: Counsel Health
competitors.funding_then: $25M Series A (a16z, GV) in October 2025 after $11M seed

competitors.name: Doctronic
competitors.traction_then: over 1 million users and 15 million conversations

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting records from labs and wearables, clinical grade AI with human review, and licensure in all 50 states are demanding but built on available models.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed practice in 50 states and patient longitudinal data help, but funded AI primary care rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A search headline claims Oura acquired Counsel Health for $625M (single unverified headline); Clara itself not acquired as of 2026.

market_need_then: Primary care access problems and rising use of chatbots for health questions; founders ran Circle Medical, giving direct demand evidence from about 1 million visits per year (company statement).

branding.domain_note: Brand site is askclara.com since clara.com was likely taken (not sourced).

identity.logo: Simple Clara wordmark; Brandfetch lists primary color #74D9BD and secondary #363636
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and forward looking: Medicine that sees further.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by Dealroom and YC social posts; patient testimonials on site.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly human name and a strong tagline, but Clara is shared by several health companies and the site fine print softens the AI doctor claim.

outcome_analysis: Clara is led by the Circle Medical team and raised a reported $12M pre-seed around its June 2026 launch, unusually large for the stage. It is too early for an outcome. Success factors cited reflect founder domain depth and a quick launch; the risks are AI medical regulation and well funded rivals.
notes: Round: the company's own site says it announced a $12M pre-seed; Dealroom (June 17, 2026) and Tryfundable agree and name investors. VCBacked lists a conflicting $3.1M profile, likely another company. One aggregator names a fourth founder, Cuauhtli Padilla, which the YC page does not, so not listed. Education not on YC page. Revenue claims for Circle Medical conflict across sources.
